findings.statement: Decoupling the recorder from the capture loop and decoding straight into the shared-memory slot reaches 5 x 1080p at 60 fps with no sensor frame lost, where the current stack reaches 53.6 fps. The prototype removes three things at once (in-loop encode, the lockstep grab gate, copy.copy), so the gain is their combined effect.
findings.evidence: prototypes/results/p8_e2e_summary.md rows p8_e2e_1080p_imdecode_msmf.json and _rep2: 59.95 / 59.95 fps, 0 / 0 sensor frames never grabbed, files == produced and consecutive, tick->written p99 16.4 / 15.2 ms; vs baseline/results/e_e2e_summary.md e_e2e_1080p_mjpeg_ui*.json: 53.56 / 53.57 fps, 964 / 964 never grabbed, p99 34.4 / 34.5 ms. Current loop: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L67-L117 (gate L67-69, put_frame L96, record L99-105). Script: p8_e2e_proto.py 1080p imdecode msmf 30.

findings.statement: Moving MJPEG decode off the capture loop (camera loop only publishes JPEG bytes; decoder threads fill the BGR ring) gives the largest timing margin at 1080p and records with about 20% CPU.
findings.evidence: p8_e2e_summary.md rows p8_e2e_1080p_imdecode_off_passthrough.json and _rep2: 59.97 fps, 0 never grabbed, decoded 60.00 fps per camera with 0 skipped, tick->written 0.8 / 1.5 / 2.9 ms, recorder CPU 19-20 %. With decode in the loop the decode step is 9.09 / 14.72 ms (median / p99) of the 16.7 ms budget (p8_e2e_1080p_imdecode_msmf.json). Script: p8_e2e_proto.py 1080p imdecode_off passthrough 30.

findings.statement: Removing copy.copy from SharedMemoryRingBuffer.put_data cuts put_frame's publish time by about 62% and nearly doubles the per-camera write ceiling, with byte-identical records.
findings.evidence: p1_write.md 1080p: cur_memcpy_putframe publish 3.085 / 4.046 ms, 238 fps vs cur_memcpy_putdata_nocopycopy 1.166 / 1.854 ms, 431 fps, inplace_verified True x5 (whole record byte-identical). Code: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/ipc/shared_memory/ring_buffer_shared_memory.py#L118-L133 (copy at L132). A flat uint8 np.copyto gives the same result (1.167 ms), so the structured-dtype assignment itself costs nothing extra.

findings.statement: cv2.VideoCapture.retrieve(image=...) can write directly into SkellyCam's existing ring slot, removing both put_frame copies and almost all publish time. This works with real cameras.
findings.evidence: p1_write.md 1080p cur_vcap_into_sk_slot: publish 0.060 ms, 0 copies, 115 fps, 8.57 ms CPU/frame vs cur_vcap_putframe publish 2.618 ms, 2 copies, 85 fps, 11.61 ms. p9_real_camera.md: in-place verified on all 4 real cameras at 720p and 1080p, 0.3-1.4 ms CPU/frame saved. Current retrieve target: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_helpers/opencv_get_frame.py#L71-L73. cv2.imdecode has no dst in OpenCV 4.12's Python binding (README P1).

findings.statement: One call, cv2.setNumThreads(1) in each camera/recorder process, cuts the real VideoRecorder's CPU at 5 x 1080p60 from 1187% to 359% (720p 506% -> 227%), with identical output and encode throughput. SkellyCam never sets it.
findings.evidence: prototypes/results/p10_msmf_threads.md (paced rows ran idle; the run is labelled provisional only because of a Defender scan at its end, load_p10_msmf_threads.json): 1187 / 359 / 563 / 619 / 750 % for default / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 threads, 124.9 Mbit/s and 0 late writes in all rows, unthrottled 114.7 vs 115.4 fps. Consistent with p5_nvenc.md (setNumThreads(2): MSMF 283 %) vs p4_mjpeg_passthrough.md (default: 939 %) and the baseline c_record.md (1207 %). grep of skellycam/ for setNumThreads: no match. Cause (OpenCV Concurrency pool busy-waiting) is an inference, not profiled.

findings.statement: The current read pattern (copy, then compare frame_number) can accept torn frames; a per-slot sequence counter (seqlock) rejected every racing read in the same test, and validated views make 5-camera reads about 70x cheaper than the current copies.
findings.evidence: p2_seqlock_read.md part A: copy_fncheck accepted 15 silent tears (latest, L=2) and 39,854-41,834 (oldest slot) with 1,068-1,846 wrong frames; seqlock rows 0 / 0. Part B: 5-camera views 0.0333 ms vs copies 1.8365 ms vs baseline get_latest_multiframe 2.3533 ms (baseline/results/b_read.md). Current reader: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/ipc/shared_memory/ring_buffer_shared_memory.py#L175-L202.

findings.statement: A gated recorder cursor makes every recording loss explicit and counted, but the stall it survives is bounded by ring length: SkellyCam's 172-slot 1080p ring absorbs 2.5 s but not 3.5 s. Today's overwrite policy would lose such frames silently if the recorder read from the ring.
findings.evidence: p3_lossless_record.md part A: L=16/64/172 tolerate 200/1000/2500 ms; at 3500 ms with L=172 overwrite lost 195 frames silently with non-consecutive output, block counted 180 sensor skips and drop counted 190 ring-full drops, both with consecutive output. Part B: real MSMF recorder, 1500 ms stall, 6005/6005 frames, 0 content mismatches in 605 checks. Note: SkellyCam's recorder does not read the ring today; it encodes in the camera loop (opencv_camera_loop.py L99-105).

findings.statement: MJPEG passthrough recording removes almost all record-path CPU and every full-frame copy on the record path, and real cameras can supply the JPEG bytes, but not through OpenCV 4.12.
findings.evidence: p4_mjpeg_passthrough.md 1080p: passthrough 35 / 28 % CPU (cameras / recorders), 0 full-frame copies, vs decode + MSMF 302 / 939 %. p9b_pyav_dshow_probe.md: PyAV dshow vcodec=mjpeg gives 100 % FF D8 packets (57-116 KB at 1080p30) on 3 of 4 cameras; p9_real_camera.md: OpenCV DSHOW CONVERT_RGB=0 still returns BGR and MSMF CAP_PROP_FORMAT=-1 is refused.

findings.statement: NVENC h264 can record 5 x 1080p60 at about 105% recorder CPU and 30 Mbit/s per camera within the 12-session limit, with about 1.5x throughput headroom. hevc_nvenc and SkellyCam's libx264 PyavVideoWriter cannot keep up at 5 x 1080p60.
findings.evidence: p5_nvenc.md: session limit 12 (13th open fails); h264_nvenc paced 105 % CPU, 29.7 Mbit/s, unthrottled slowest 89 fps (sum 447); hevc_nvenc unthrottled slowest 56 fps, paced backlog 693 ms median; pyav_libx264 2442 % CPU, slowest 46 fps, 319 sensor frames lost paced. p7_topology.md h264_nvenc aggregate 407-426 fps. PyavVideoWriter: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/recorders/videos/pyav_video_writer.py#L3-L39. NVENC adds p99 tick->written of 103-218 ms (blocking encode calls), so it needs the decoupled recorder.

findings.statement: The UI build can be taken off the event loop (which also serves the recording start/stop handlers) by reading slot views and running resize + JPEG in a thread pool. This reaches 60 payloads/s at 1080p with under 0.1 ms of loop blocking.
findings.evidence: p6_ui_path.md 1080p: view_proto_threads_poll2ms 60.1/s, build 1.96 / 3.03 ms, loop blocked 0.04 / 0.07 ms; current pattern cur_copy_real 51.8/s with the loop blocked 8.28 / 10.11 ms; baseline d_ui.md 46.0/s. Relay: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/api/websocket/websocket_server.py#L189-L212. Payload builder: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/types/frontend_payload_bytearray.py#L41

findings.statement: Pixel work releases the GIL and scales as well in threads as in processes, but per-frame pure-Python control work does not. Per-camera control loops should stay in separate processes; decode, encode and UI jobs can use threads.
findings.evidence: p7_topology.md: imdecode x4.60 threads vs x4.90 processes, simplejpeg x5.00 vs x5.05, py_overhead x1.03 vs x4.97 (median of 5 repetitions).

findings.statement: libjpeg-turbo decoding straight into the slot (simplejpeg) is 1.6x faster than cv2.imdecode plus a copy at 1080p, and gives the most decode headroom in the camera loop.
findings.evidence: p1_write.md 1080p: p_simplejpeg_into_slot 4.680 ms, 212 fps vs p_imdecode_copyslot 7.515 ms, 132 fps; p8_e2e_summary.md p8_e2e_1080p_simplejpeg_msmf.json decode 5.82 / 9.51 ms vs imdecode 9.09 / 14.72 ms.

findings.statement: On OpenCV's DSHOW backend, grab() returns immediately and the wait for the frame happens inside retrieve(). SkellyCam's grab timestamps therefore mark when grab was called, not when the frame arrived. This is an open question for multi-camera synchronisation.
findings.evidence: p9_real_camera.md: grab median 0.00-0.01 ms, retrieve+publish median about 32 ms at 30 fps on all 4 cameras. Timestamps around grab(): https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_helpers/opencv_get_frame.py#L53-L55. Measured in a standalone loop, not SkellyCam's.

limitations: Real-camera 5 x 60 fps was not possible: 4 UVC cameras are attached and none delivered more than 30.1 fps tonight (p9_real_camera.md, p9b_pyav_dshow_probe.md). All 5 x 60 results use the synthetic FakeSensor (free-running, latest-frame-wins) with q90 synthetic JPEGs (540 KB at 1080p, larger than real frames of 57-116 KB).

P8 removes SkellyCam's lockstep grab gate as well as the in-loop encode and copy.copy, so its gain cannot be attributed to one change. Cross-camera timing spread of free-running cameras was not measured, and timestamp-based grouping is an open question.

P10 is labelled provisional by the idle rule (Windows Defender scanned files at the end of the run). Its paced rows ran with background <= 6.1%. The cause of the thread-count effect (OpenCV Concurrency pool busy-waiting) is inferred, not profiled.
Whether DSHOW decodes MJPEG on the calling thread or on a graph thread could not be separated (P9: wait and decode both sit inside retrieve()).
The SeqRing seqlock relies on x86-64 store ordering and single-instruction int64 stores. It is not portable to ARM without fences.
P8 recorders release a slot only after write()/encode() returns. This is safe for MSMF and PyAV here (P3 content check 0/605) but relies on each encoder copying its input.

No browser was attached in P6, so websocket send and browser decode are excluded. P6 rates with 10 ms polling vary with timer phase (same row 53.0 vs 57.8/s at 1080p, 60.0 vs 42.6/s at 720p across the two venvs).
simplejpeg encode was not tuned (larger payloads than cv2.imencode); PyTurboJPEG could not be tested (DLL missing).
P3 models a stall as a sleep; no slow-disk / full pSLC-cache test was run. A spill-to-disk policy was not prototyped.
P4/P5 unthrottled disk MB/s reflect the OS write cache, not sustained NVMe throughput. Passthrough file sizes with real cameras are extrapolated (about 5-9x smaller).
Copies inside MSMF, NVENC upload, DSHOW and FFmpeg are not countable from Python.
